title: onprem carry-on notes
body:
Quick carry-on for onsite run — rough, noisy, keep portable. Intended for me + whoever gets looped in the morning.

03/12 AM: arrived at customer DC (Rack 7). Walkthrough notes + immediate TODOs.

Top priorities today:
- Verify rack power feeds (A/B) and lock schedule for PDUs — customer said circuits red-tagged, double-check label vs handed-over diagram.
- PXE image boot and puppet/ansible baseline (centos-8 -> rhel8 image as customer requested compliance).
- KMS integration smoke: check ability to reach customer HSM IPs from bastion (perimeter egress rule).
- Bring up single-node sandbox for acceptance tests (no autofailover until we sign-off).

Onsite observations / environment reminders:
- Rack 7 unit 20: Dell R750xd, 2xA100 80GB each. RAID controller set to HBA — good.
- Network: leaf-switch L-14 interface to top-of-rack uses VLANs 110 (mgmt), 210 (app), 310 (storage). Customer firewall drops 443->kms-host unless source is bastion IP (asked them to whitelist 10.240.8.12).
- No dedicated NTP; they're using internal GPS stratum-1. Confirmed time skew < 2s.

Commands / snippets I used:
- quick check for HSM reachability: nc -vz 10.11.22.9 1792 (timed out initially)
- curl from bastion to KMS endpoint: curl -v --cacert /tmp/customer-root.pem https://kms.internal.example/v1/health
- PXE boot monitor: tail -f /var/log/pxe/tftp.log | grep "dhcp"

Failure modes encountered / blockers:
- Blocker A: KMS port 1792 blocked on customer perimeter for hosts in VLAN 110. Temporary workaround: tunnel via bastion (ssh -L 1792:10.11.22.9:1792 ec2-bastion) but we need permanent firewall rule. Ticketed JIRA-5821.
- Blocker B: Installer failed on node03 at package stage (rpm dependency conflict with customer-supplied repo). Re-pointed yum to internal mirror and disabled vendor repo. Need follow-up with cust infra to audit their repo mirroring.
- Minor: SELinux issues during container run (denied writes on /var/lib/cache). Set to permissive for sandbox; don't forget to revert.

Acceptance checklist (single-node smoke):
[ ] OS image booted and patched (kernel >= 4.18)
[ ] Docker + containerd versions consistent with runbook
[ ] KMS handshake succeeds without tunnel
[ ] Model artifact pulled from artifactory (10.200.4.8)
[ ] Inference container starts, responds on health endpoint /healthz within 200ms
[ ] Basic gen test: echo \"hello\" -> model returns something coherent (sanity only)

Notes for handover to customer ops:
- If you need to whitelist, add source CIDR 10.240.8.0/24 to allow KMS ports 1792 and 443 to HSM cluster (10.11.22.8/9).
- Port 2379 (etcd) should remain internal — do not expose to management VLAN.
- Keep NTP pointing to GPS; otherwise certificates for internal CA will fail automated renewal checks.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can customer rotate KMS certs during patch window? Who is the owner? (asked Ops lead but not confirmed)
- Confirm SLA window for rebooting prod nodes — they said overnight only but we need 1-hour window for restart tests.
- Ask security: are we allowed to enable passwordless sudo for 'deploy' user or do we need to keep sudo via ticket approval?

Handy links & quick refs I left in shell history:
- runbook: confluence.company.com/display/INF/Private+Deploy+Runbook#preflight
- infra PR to review: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/789
- ticket: https://jira.company.com/browse/JIRA-5821

Mini checklist for tomorrow AM (priority order):
1) confirm firewall rule change scheduled (Ops said 10:30am slot)
2) re-run KMS handshake test from node03 (without SSH tunnel)
3) finalize SELinux policy for inference container (generate allow rules instead of leaving permissive)
4) run end-to-end model pull + quick inference accuracy check with sample prompts (use customer sample set small.json)

Random scraps / shorthand (for my brain):
- bring extra RJ45 cables (CAT6A)
- remember to ask about PDU tagging system (they had handwritten labels)
- coffee stop map: floor 2 kitchenette closed on weekends

Status: stopping now — syncing logs to confluence draft and uploading relevant tarball to artifacts. Will re-open this note tomorrow morning and move completed checks to final runbook.
summary: Onsite personal notes + todo for private onprem run (KMS firewall block main blocker).
